headlines.summary: GM narrowed its 2026 earnings guidance and raised its adjusted automotive free cash flow outlook after beating Wall Street’s third-quarter estimates.
headlines.article_text: General Motors (GM) earnings Q3 2026 Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points General Motors beat Wall Street’s expectations on the top- and bottom-lines. The Detroit automaker raised its free cash flow expectations and narrowed its 2026 full-year guidance. GM also announced a new multiyear stock buyback of $20 billion, but didn’t give a specific timeframe for the repurchase. In this article GM Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT The General Motors global headquarters in Detroit, Jan. 12, 2026. Jeff Kowalsky | Bloomberg | Getty Images DETROIT — General Motors narrowed its 2026 earnings guidance and raised its free cash flow expectations after beating Wall Street's third-quarter expectations. The Detroit automaker also announced a new multiyear stock buyback of $20 billion after GM completed a $6 billion share repurchase program that was announced in January. GM did not disclose a specific time to complete the program. Here's how GM performed in the third quarter, compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG: Earnings per share: $3.70 adjusted vs. $3.63 expected Revenue: $50.02 billion vs. $48.7 billion expected The new guidance includes adjusted earnings before interest and taxes of between $14.5 billion and $15.5 billion, or $12.75 to $13.75 adjusted earnings per share, and adjusted automotive free cash flow of between $11.5 billion and $12.5 billion. That compares with its raised guidance from July that included adjusted EBIT of between $14 billion and $16 billion, or $12 to $14 adjusted EPS, and adjusted automotive free cash flow of $9.5 billion to $11.5 billion. "I think the market's been pretty consistent from what we've said all year," GM CFO Paul Jacobson told CNBC's Phil LeBeau . "Our fourth quarter's going to be down sequentially. ... I think the fact that we're able to hold our guidance in the face of that late inflationary pressure in the year is another sign of the GM team executing really well." GM stock was off roughly 5% during premarket trading despite the earnings beats. Wall Street analysts were mixed before the report on whether GM would raise its guidance Tuesday amid concerns of slowing sales and rising commodity costs. GM on Tuesday said it expects commodity inflation costs to be around $2 billion, which was the high end of its previous guidance. That includes higher costs for logistics and dynamic random-access memory, or DRAM, chips that are impacting multiple industries . While the inflationary costs were at the automaker's high end of guidance, GM said its gross tariff costs are expected to be at the low end of its expected $2.5 billion to $3.5 billion range. Warranty costs are expected to be at high end between $1 billion and $1.5 billion, GM said. Jacobson said vehicle pricing is relatively flat as inflationary costs continue to increase. He said the company would assess where consumers are in the coming year when deciding if it should pass costs along by raising prices more than normal. "GM is performing well, and we are working hard to continue our momentum despite growing inflationary pressures through strategic investments in new products and services, and through improved quality and operating efficiency," GM CEO Mary Barra said Tuesday in a letter to shareholders. The automaker also said the costs of its pullback in all-electric vehicles announced last year were "substantially completed," saying it has recorded $11.2 billion in such charges since the second half of last year, including paying $4.6 billion of $7.4 billion in cash through the third quarter. The company's net income attributed to stockholders was $3.3 billion during the third quarter, up roughly $2 billion from a year earlier. GM's North American operations continued to lead the automaker's results, accounting for $3.6 billion of its $4.1 billion in adjusted EBIT results during the third quarter. GM's 2025 third-quarter results included $48.59 billion in revenue, net income attributable to stockholders of $1.3 billion and earnings per share of $2.80 adjusted. headlines.title: Best Buy launches new gaming hub ahead of 'Zelda' and 'Grand Theft Auto VI'
headlines.summary: Best Buy is launching a new gaming experience for customers as it leans into the business ahead of this fall's big launches.
headlines.article_text: Best Buy launches Gamers beta with IGN Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Best Buy is launching a new gaming experience for customers as it leans into the fast-growing business, the company told CNBC exclusively. The announcement comes ahead of some of this year's biggest launches, including "Grand Theft Auto VI" next month. Chief Revenue Officer Patrick McGinnis told CNBC the timing of the launch is "pretty perfect," though the new experience has been in the works for over a year. The company has previously said gaming is a large driver of its overall performance each quarter. In this article BBY Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A Best Buy store in Los Angeles, California, Aug. 27, 2026. Justin Sullivan | Getty Images Best Buy is tapping further into a growing customer cohort: gamers. Chief Revenue Officer Patrick McGinnis told CNBC exclusively that the electronics retailer is launching a new experience Tuesday for customers featuring gaming content, new technology and special offers, among other features. The online destination is called Best Buy Gamers and is launching in a beta version. "Gamers are a customer that are really like no other in terms of their passion for not just the tech, the titles, but also how they want to work with each other as a community," McGinnis said. "So for us, being relevant for that customer wherever and whenever they want to interact with the thing that they love is really important." Best Buy says tens of millions of gamers shop at the retailer each year, including trying out games in the store and seeking advice from in-store experts. The new gaming experience, created in partnership with video game website IGN, will offer members gaming articles and reviews, live Best Buy event updates for launches and deals on new technology. The announcement comes ahead of some of the biggest launches in gaming this year, including the Nov. 5 release of "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time," a remake from Nintendo , and the Nov. 19 launch of Take-Two Interactive 's highly anticipated "Grand Theft Auto VI." McGinnis said the timing of the rollout is "pretty perfect" given the slate of new video games over the next month, though Best Buy has been developing the new platform for over a year. "We want to be relevant for our gaming customers, not just during the important, big tentpole periods of the calendar, like when we have these big gaming launches coming up, but really every day," he said. "We want to be there when they discover new titles and connect with the community, and not just when they're buying a big console or a new gaming title." Best Buy has been leaning into gaming as it sees growing demand from its customers. For its fiscal first-quarter results reported in May, the company said gaming and computing was one of its biggest drivers of growth. On a call with analysts to discuss Best Buy's fiscal second quarter in August, incoming CEO Jason Bonfig said the company expects that demand for "Grand Theft Auto VI" will boost the gaming category. Best Buy has been looking for growth drivers as the retailer tries to revitalize its business performance under Bonfig. The company has seen slumping sales and was hit by tariffs and lower consumer confidence, among other factors. Tapping into gaming could help revitalize the retailer. McGinnis said the new gamer experience is an example of the company's strategic goals coming together. "If you think about what those priorities are, the Gamers [beta] community is definitely a way that we're expanding and growing our reach, reaching that gaming customer," he said. "Providing a place for them to again pursue what they're most passionate about certainly is elevating our experience." Best Buy is also leaning into in-store experiences around gaming, starting with a location in Torrance, California, next month, where Sony , Nintendo and Microsoft will come together to offer gaming experiences and activations for customers. With the combination of physical retail and the online platform, McGinnis said, Best Buy hopes to sit at the intersection of technology, entertainment and culture within the gaming community. He said the company plans to tweak its new online experience based on feedback from its customers and continue innovating to meet its audience where it is, especially as the gaming segment continues to be one of the company's strongest performers. "We recognize the gaming customer as incredibly passionate and wants to engage with what they love in a lot of different ways," he said. "There's observations of gaps that exist in the places and spaces where gamers are engaged, and we thought that we could build something that would really complement what they're engaging with today from a social platform perspective, not to replace those types of experiences in any way, shape or form." headlines.summary: Data center campuses house the servers that power AI and cloud computing.
headlines.article_text: HSBC CEO on data center financing amid AI borrowing spree Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery told CNBC that data center deals hinge on the quality of tenants and contract pricing. Global data center spending could reach $7 trillion by 2030, McKinsey estimates. Hyperscalers’ growing bond issuance is adding to competition for financing, Mohamed El-Erian has said. In this article HSBC Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:53 01:53 HSBC CEO on AI's business potential: 'It's going to be transformational' Squawk Box Europe AI is a transformational technology worth investing in — but investors must be selective when investing in data centers, according to the head of one of the world's biggest banks. Speaking to CNBC's Dan Murphy on Tuesday, HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery called artificial intelligence "a major enabler to re-engineer and reimagine all our businesses, all our activities." "It's going to put a lot of power back in the hands of our colleagues because of the level of productivity it gives them, so it's going to be transformational, and we're certainly very much on a journey to adopt it," he said, adding that AI would help to "re-engineer the bank." But when it comes to investing in infrastructure underpinning the technology, he advised discernment over an all-in approach. "One has to be selective," Elhedery said. "You have to look at the quality of the tenancy agreements. You have to look at the pricing of these contracts. Not all of them are of that level of virtuosity that you can support strongly. Some of them may be more challenging." HSBC was ranked as the seventh-largest bank in the world and the biggest lender in Europe by S&P Global last year, with assets worth close to $3 trillion. The bank — headquartered in London — is both a financier and operator of data centers. In its 2025 annual report, HSBC said it intends to become "the leading bank for fast-growing transition ecosystems," noting that its customer base spans areas including data centers and the AI sector. Data center campuses house the servers that power AI and cloud computing, and have seen a multibillion-dollar boom in recent years. Global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030, according to McKinsey, with Big Tech increasingly tapping private credit and taking on debt to fund the development of the facilities. But AI borrowing is becoming a source of tension in financial markets, as the cost of capital soars and corporations add to huge debt piles as they race to finance AI and the build-out of data centers. Debt-hungry AI companies face increased risk as bond yields spike Speaking at LSEG and Eurasia Group's GZERO Summit in London earlier this month, Mohamed El-Erian, chief economic adviser of Allianz and former CEO of PIMCO, highlighted the competition for financing between governments and AI-related companies as a source of pressure in bond markets. "Governments are borrowing what they're borrowing, plus they're refinancing debt at a higher level of rates," he said. "[And] you have hyperscalers who last year raised $200 billion in bond financing, and are probably going to raise a trillion in bond financing this year. They are yield insensitive. They are spread insensitive because they are betting on something that is truly transformational." Bond yields issued by various major economies have hit multi-decade highs in 2026, amid concerns around elevated government deficits and mounting debt levels alongside fears of sticky inflation and more hawkish central banks. JPMorgan Chase estimated earlier this year that $4.1 trillion in AI-related debt will be issued by the end of the decade, as data center and other AI-adjacent companies splurge on building capacity. headlines.article_text: Walmart launches Walmart+, Sam's Club Plus joint membership Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Walmart is now offering a joint Walmart+ membership with Sam's Club Plus for $120 per year as the retailer further leans into convenience. Both stores will continue to offer standalone membership options. The announcement comes as Walmart has been emphasizing value to grow sales, especially as consumers face high gas and food prices. In this article WMT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Sam's Club and Walmart stores. Walmart on Tuesday announced a new joint membership combining its namesake chain and its subsidiary Sam's Club, as the retailer leans further into convenience and value to win over cash-strapped shoppers. The membership, which combines Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus, will cost $120 per year, according to the company. That price is nearly $100 less than buying individual annual memberships to each retailer, though there is no monthly payment option for the new deal. Both stores will continue to offer standalone options. "We're giving people a reason to expect more from their memberships," Walmart CEO John Furner said in a statement. "For $120 a year, we're raising expectations for what a membership can deliver: more money in their pockets and more time to call their own." The membership gives customers access to Sam's Club warehouses, free delivery from both chains, a subscription to Peacock or Paramount+ streaming services, gas savings and 2% Sam's Club cash on eligible purchases. Customers who already have accounts at both stores can link their accounts to receive the discount. While Walmart's customers often shop for routine, everyday essentials, Sam's Club warehouses offer more opportunity to stock up on bulk purchases. A joint membership could allow the store models to complement one another, according to the company. The announcement comes as Walmart bets on convenience to drive sales, especially as consumer wallets are squeezed by high gas and food prices. In August, as Walmart reported fiscal second-quarter earnings, the company raised its outlook for the year, with Chief Financial Officer John David Rainey telling CNBC that consumer spending remained strong despite higher fuel prices. Even so, its stock fell at the time as its sales outlook disappointed Wall Street. Rainey said in August that the company was lowering prices across various categories, including beef, adding that it's well positioned to weather economic uncertainty because of its emphasis on value and its scale. Meanwhile, Sam's Club saw a 26% increase in e-commerce sales in the fiscal second quarter, driven by increased transactions and membership growth. The retailer, which also operates its own gas stations, reported net sales of $25.7 billion, including fuel, during that period. The membership business — which is part of Walmart's push to grow sales with higher profit margins — is already strong. Walmart reported a 17% increase globally in revenue from its membership in the fiscal second quarter with Walmart+ net adds notching a record second-quarter high. For Sam's Club, that revenue number grew 6%. Walmart added Tuesday that employees at both stores will also receive joint memberships as part of their benefits. The company said any costs related to the changes in the membership program are not expected to materially impact the company's fiscal third-quarter or full-year guidance.
